internalInconsistencies.description: Assets table shows Main Residence £430,000, Cash £17,000, Total £447,000. Liabilities show Mortgage £70,000. Net Asset Value = £447,000 - £70,000 = £377,000. This is stated correctly. However, the narrative later states 'Currently, your assets are below your allowance of £500,000 meaning you have no Inheritance Tax liability.' The £500,000 threshold refers to the Nil Rate Band (NRB) of £325,000 plus Main Residence Nil Rate Band (RNRB) of £175,000 = £500,000 total. The client's net assets of £377,000 are indeed below £500,000. But the narrative then states 'However, on receipt of the inheritance this will take you over the limit.' The inheritance is £350,000, so total would be £377,000 + £350,000 = £727,000, which exceeds £500,000. This is consistent. However, the IHT analysis does not account for the fact that pensions are currently outside the estate (as stated) but will be included from 6 April 2027. The pension values (Quilter c. £260,000 + True Potential £46,672.80 + Nest £21,272.64 = c. £327,945) would add significantly to the taxable estate from that date, but this is not quantified in the IHT summary.
valuesObserved: Pension values not included in current IHT calculation but will be from 6 April 2027
